version.changelog:
Initial release of Pixel Familiar Identity — an AI agent framework for autonomous, revenue-focused business operations.

- Provides a complete SOUL.md template for CEO agent identity.
- Features revenue-oriented decision frameworks.
- Includes multi-agent coordination and delegation protocols.
- Offers model routing, identity, and voice guidelines.
- Suitable for running AI agents in real business contexts.

vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: pixel-familiar-soul
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle provides a comprehensive identity and orchestration framework (SOUL.md) for an AI agent persona named 'Pixel'. It focuses on task delegation, model routing, and business logic without any indicators of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or unauthorized execution. Notably, it includes explicit 'Approval Gates' that restrict the agent from performing financial transactions or cold outreach without human intervention.

llm.summary: Instruction-only 'CEO' identity that is mostly coherent with its purpose but grants broad autonomous authority, references cross-agent file reads and external models without declaring required credentials, and contains directives that could cause wide-ranging actions — review before use.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (an agent 'identity' / CEO orchestrator) aligns with the provided instructions (delegation, routing, escalation). However it calls out use of specific external models (Anthropic Claude, 'GPT 5.4', MiniMax) and platform APIs (sessions_send, sessions_spawn, session_status) but lists no required credentials or environment variables — an incoherence that may be benign if the platform supplies these, but should be clarified.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and SOUL.md instruct the agent to read shared-context files (agents/shared-context/*) and MEMORY.md curation, to delegate broadly via sessions_send, and to surface detailed blocker context to 'Scott'. These instructions allow reading and transmitting cross-agent context and potentially sensitive session data. The broad rule 'If it doesn't move money, just do it' grants wide operational latitude that could result in unexpected external actions (outreach, account creation, posting) unless platform-level safeguards exist.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — lowest installation risk. Nothing is written to disk by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials, yet explicitly instructs using named external models and session APIs. Either the platform provides these transparently (which would be normal) or the skill omitted necessary credential requirements. Also, the approval-gates list suggests the agent will perform many actions that may require additional service tokens (email, CRM, messaging) — these are not declared here.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (good) but the agent is given broad autonomous authority for non-money actions and top-tier escalation role. Combined with cross-agent delegation APIs, this gives a high operational blast radius if the agent is allowed to act autonomously. The skill does not request persistent system privileges, but its behavioral rules permit broad side-effects across other agents and shared data.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is an instruction-only identity template for an autonomous 'CEO' agent. Before installing: 1) Confirm what platform APIs (sessions_send, session_status, sessions_spawn) actually do and what permissions they grant; who (or what) receives delegated messages. 2) Verify whether your platform supplies the named external models (Claude, GPT 5.4) or whether API keys/tokens are needed — if keys are required, decide where/how they will be stored and whether to limit access. 3) Consider restricting or removing the rule 'If it doesn't move money, just do it' — it grants broad authority to take many actions that could have side effects (posting, outreach, account changes). 4) Audit and limit which shared-context files the agent can read (agents/shared-context/*, MEMORY.md) to avoid accidental exposure of secrets. 5) Test the identity in a sandboxed agent environment with logging and an approval gate for outbound communications and integrations. 6) If you are not comfortable with the agent autonomously delegating work or transmitting cross-agent context, do not enable autonomous invocation or ask the author to narrow the scope and explicitly declare required credentials and channels.
